genZNote: Oxidase positive is the whole plot twist — it's the test that keeps this yellow skin commensal from being mistaken for Staph.

habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Also widespread in soil, dust, and water

microscopy.appearance: Gram-positive cocci in tetrads or irregular clusters

culture.colonyMorphology: Small to medium, smooth, convex colonies

biochemicalTests.result: Susceptible (distinguishes from Staphylococcus, which is resistant)

identificationClues: Yellow-pigmented, catalase-positive Gram-positive coccus in tetrads
Oxidase positive — the key test separating it from Staphylococcus (oxidase negative)
Obligate aerobe, unlike facultatively anaerobic Staphylococcus

diseases: Rarely pathogenic; occasional opportunistic infections (bacteremia, endocarditis, catheter-related infection) in immunocompromised patients
virulenceFactors: None of major clinical significance — low-virulence commensal
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: A frequent skin/environmental contaminant in blood and other cultures, most often clinically insignificant
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Oxidase and bacitracin testing reliably distinguish Micrococcus from the more clinically significant, morphologically similar Staphylococcus

examFacts.importantDisease: Rarely pathogenic — normal skin flora and common culture contaminant
examFacts.importantTest: Oxidase test (positive) and bacitracin susceptibility distinguish it from Staphylococcus
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Yellow-pigmented, oxidase-positive Gram-positive coccus in tetrads — oxidase positivity is the key differentiator from Staphylococcus
